newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica announces apparel industry bailout.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica announces apparel industry bailout.

text.p: The Jamaican government Tuesday announced a 15-month, multi-million dollar bail-out for the island's struggling garment industry.
The bailout came several seeks after a number of garment factories announced they were closing, putting over 1,000 people out of work.

Industry minister Dr. Paul Robertson said the island's 180 garment factories would get subsidies equivalent to 5 percent of their operating costs between January and March. The three-month disbursements were expected to total $1.14 million.
The assistance will continue for the full length of the 1997-98 financial year, which begins April 1, Robertson said.
He said the full amount of the bailout would be determined after a comprehensive study of the industry is completed in January, but would likely be in the region of $4.6 million.
Exports between January and October this year declined by 5 percent, according to garment industry officials, although no dollar amounts were made available.
Exports for the first nine months of 1996 stood at $377 million, down 12 percent. The apparel sector is the country's second-largest export earner after bauxite and alumina.

Total employment in the industry has fallen from 36,000 two years ago to 21,000 now. Industry officials say Mexico has become a far more attractive site for investment due to the North American Free Trade Agreement, while operating costs in Jamaica are now among the highest in the region.
